stem: An industrial engineering study measures the assembly time (seconds) for a sample of 30 factory workers. The sample mean is 239.6 sec with a sample standard deviation of 52.2 sec. However, 3 of the 30 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 27 observations have a mean of 231.6 sec and standard deviation of 37.9 sec. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 239.6, 95% CI = [220.1, 259.1]. Without outliers: mean = 231.6, 95% CI = [217.0, 246.2]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [217.0, 259.1]. Point estimate: 235.6 sec.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [217.0, 259.1].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
